newsitem.title: USA: Rocket blasts-off with European TV satellite.
newsitem.headline: Rocket blasts-off with European TV satellite.

text.p: A European television satellite roared into space on Thursday, riding atop a Lockheed Martin Corp. Atlas 2 rocket.
The slender white rocket climbed from its launch pad at Cape Canaveral Air Station at 3:47 p.m. EST (2047 GMT).

The Hot Bird 2 satellite, owned by the international Eutelsat consortium, was placed into an egg-shaped preliminary orbit about 29 minutes later. It was scheduled to fire its on-board rocket motor later to reach a final orbit 22,300 miles (35,680 km) above the equator.
The liftoff was delayed from Nov. 13, three times because of bad weather and once to accommodate the launch of the U.S. space shuttle Columbia.

The $200 million satellite will broadcast 45 digital and 20 analog television channels to homes across Europe and as far east as Kazakhstan. It is the first of four similar satellites built for Eutelsat by Matra Marconi Space.
It was the 26th consecutive successful launch for the Atlas rocket, which started life in the 1950s as an intercontinental ballistic missile.
